package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of Envoy Proxy contain a denial-of-service (DoS) vulnerability (CVE-2022-29225) in the Brotli and GZip decompression filters, allowing attackers to exhaust system memory by sending highly-compressed files that decompress to extremely large sizes, leading to performance degradation or process crashes.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (upon receiving HTTP requests with compressed payloads)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code decompresses Brotli-encoded HTTP payloads and accumulates all decompressed data into a single buffer without enforcing a maximum size, leading to unbounded memory allocation and potential process crash.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unbounded memory allocation based on attacker-controlled input is a classic vector for denial-of-service attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal decompression should enforce reasonable output size limits to prevent resource exhaustion; here, no such limit is present.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate decompression of large files, but always with output size or resource limits.
key_indicators: Memory allocation proportional to decompressed size

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a Brotli-compressed file (Brotli bomb) that decompresses to a very large size.
attack_chain.leads_to: File is sent to Envoy Proxy via HTTP request.

attack_chain.action: Envoy Proxy receives the HTTP request and, due to its configuration, invokes the Brotli decompression filter.
The Brotli decompression filter decompresses the payload into an unbounded buffer, consuming excessive memory.
attack_chain.leads_to: System memory exhaustion, performance degradation, or process crash (DoS).

behavioral_signatures: Unusually large memory allocation during HTTP request processing
Decompression of Brotli or GZip payloads with no output size limit
Process crash or restart following large compressed payloads
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests with large Brotli-compressed payloads
Repeated requests from a single source with compressed data
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Envoy Proxy configurations for enabled Brotli or GZip decompression filters. Analyze memory usage patterns for sudden spikes during HTTP request processing. Inspect logs for process crashes or restarts following large compressed payloads. Use SCA tools to identify vulnerable Envoy versions and flag configurations that enable decompression without output size limits.
